title: Control Board Thermistor Failure
shortDescription: The electronic control board has detected a thermistor or temperature sensor fault.
fullDescription:
Error F1 on a Whirlpool microwave indicates the control board has lost communication with the temperature sensor (thermistor) or has received an out-of-range signal. The sensor monitors cavity temperature during sensor cook cycles.

A faulty thermistor, damaged wiring harness, or failed control board are the typical root causes. The microwave may refuse to start, beep repeatedly, or abort cycles partway through.

Unplug the unit for 5 minutes to attempt a reset. If the code returns, the thermistor or control board will need replacement.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the microwave for 5 minutes, then restore power.

fixSteps.title: Inspect thermistor wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Access the control panel and check the thermistor connector for secure seating.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the thermistor with an OEM part if resistance is out of spec.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the control board needs replacement or if you are uncomfortable working near the high-voltage capacitor.

faq.q: Can I use the microwave with F1 showing?
faq.a: No. The unit will typically lock out cooking functions until the fault clears.

title: Keypad / Touch Panel Shorted
shortDescription: A stuck or shorted key has been detected on the keypad.
fullDescription:
The F2 code appears when the control board detects a keypad input held for more than 60 seconds, which it interprets as a short. Moisture, grease, or a worn membrane can all cause this.

Clean the keypad first, then inspect the ribbon cable connecting the touch panel to the control board. If cleaning and reseating the ribbon does not clear the code, the touch panel assembly is likely defective.

A damaged keypad rarely repairs itself and replacement is the standard fix.

fixSteps.title: Clean keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the touch panel with a soft dry cloth to remove grease and moisture.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open the control panel and reseat the keypad ribbon into the control board.

fixSteps.title: Replace touch panel
fixSteps.instruction: If code persists, install a new touch panel assembly.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if reseating the ribbon does not help and you are uncertain about discharging the capacitor.
videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool microwave F2 error keypad fix

faq.q: Why does F2 appear after cleaning?
faq.a: Moisture trapped under the membrane can short contacts. Let it air dry for several hours.

title: Humidity Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The humidity (steam) sensor has reported an out-of-range reading.
fullDescription:
F3 indicates the humidity sensor that monitors steam during sensor cook cycles is returning an invalid reading. The sensor is usually mounted in the cavity exhaust path.

Grease buildup on the sensor mesh is the most common cause. Wiring faults and a failed sensor are next most likely.

After cleaning, verify the harness is seated. If the error persists, replace the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor area
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the exhaust vent and sensor mesh inside the cavity with a damp cloth.

fixSteps.title: Check harness
fixSteps.instruction: Open the top grille and ensure the sensor connector is secure.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new humidity sensor if resistance checks fail.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if cleaning and sensor replacement do not resolve the code.
videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool microwave F3 humidity sensor fix

faq.q: Can I still use manual cook?
faq.a: Often yes — only sensor cycles are disabled until F3 clears.

title: Shorted Temperature Probe
shortDescription: The meat probe circuit is shorted to ground.
fullDescription:
F4 means the control board sees a short in the temperature probe circuit. If the probe is not currently used, the jack itself may have shorted or corroded.

Check for foreign debris or moisture in the probe jack. Inspect the probe cord if one is inserted.

If the jack is clean and the probe tests good, the control board may be at fault.

causes.cause: Debris or moisture in probe jack

fixSteps.title: Remove probe
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug any inserted probe and clean the jack with contact cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Test probe
fixSteps.instruction: Check probe resistance against spec at room temperature.

fixSteps.title: Replace probe or board
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the probe first, then the control board if needed.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the issue is traced to the main control board.

faq.q: Does F4 appear without a probe attached?
faq.a: Yes — debris in the jack can trigger it even without a probe inserted.

title: Open Temperature Probe
shortDescription: The temperature probe circuit is open.
fullDescription:
F5 is the inverse of F4 — the control board sees no continuity in the probe circuit. A damaged probe or disconnected internal wire is the usual cause.

If no probe is inserted, suspect an internal wiring fault between the jack and control board.

Replace the probe first since it is the cheaper part to rule out.

fixSteps.title: Test probe
fixSteps.instruction: Measure probe resistance — open circuit means replace.

fixSteps.title: Check harness
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the probe jack harness at the control board.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if internal wiring is damaged.
videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool microwave F5 probe open fix

faq.q: Why does F5 appear with no probe in use?
faq.a: The jack can show open if internal wiring is loose behind the control panel.

title: Line Voltage Fault
shortDescription: The microwave detects out-of-range line voltage.
fullDescription:
F6 appears when the control board measures AC line voltage outside the expected 108-132 V range. Power surges, brownouts, and faulty outlets are common external causes.

Internally, a failed line filter, noise capacitor, or control board can also trigger it.

Verify outlet voltage with a meter. If line voltage is good and the error persists, the control board is the likely suspect.

fixSteps.title: Test outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Measure AC voltage at the outlet under load.

fixSteps.title: Inspect line filter
fixSteps.instruction: Discharge capacitor and inspect the line filter for burn marks.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro or electrician — this code can involve live-voltage diagnosis and a charged capacitor.
videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool microwave F6 line voltage fix

faq.q: Is F6 caused by my home wiring?
faq.a: Often yes. Bad neutrals, overloaded circuits, or surges can trigger it.

title: Internal Communication Error
shortDescription: The control boards failed to communicate with each other.
fullDescription:
F7 appears when the user interface board and main control board lose communication. Loose harness connections and firmware faults are the usual triggers.

Power cycle first. If the error returns, inspect the ribbon cable between the boards.

Persistent F7 usually requires replacing the main control board.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes and try again.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat ribbon cable between UI and main board.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if reseating harnesses does not restore communication.
videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool microwave F7 communication error fix

faq.q: Does a firmware update fix F7?
faq.a: No — microwaves do not have user-accessible firmware updates.

title: Over-Temperature Shutdown
shortDescription: The magnetron thermal protector tripped due to overheating.
fullDescription:
F8 indicates the magnetron or cavity thermal cutoff opened because internal temperature exceeded safe limits. Blocked vents, a failing fan, or a shorted magnetron are typical root causes.

Let the unit cool for at least 30 minutes. Confirm the cooling fan runs when power is applied and the vents are unobstructed.

If the unit overheats again, the magnetron is almost certainly degraded.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and let the microwave cool 30 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Clean charcoal and grease filters, verify rear exhaust is unobstructed.

fixSteps.title: Test fan
fixSteps.instruction: Verify cooling fan operates during cooking.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the magnetron is suspect — high-voltage section requires trained handling.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep using the microwave?
faq.a: No — continued overheating can damage the magnetron and cabinet wiring.

title: Door Switch Fault
shortDescription: A door interlock switch is not reporting the expected state.
fullDescription:
F9 indicates the monitor switch or primary/secondary interlock switches are inconsistent. This is a safety-critical circuit — the microwave will not run until it clears.

A misaligned door, broken hook, or failed switch are typical causes.

Inspect door hooks for damage and test each switch for continuity with the door closed and open.

fixSteps.title: Inspect door
fixSteps.instruction: Check door for sag and broken plastic hooks.

fixSteps.title: Test switches
fixSteps.instruction: Discharge capacitor and test each interlock switch for continuity.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you are not comfortable discharging the high-voltage capacitor.
videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool microwave F9 door switch fix

faq.a: It is a safety lockout. Do not bypass interlocks — microwaves can emit radiation if switches are defeated.

title: ERC Memory Error
shortDescription: The control board EEPROM memory is corrupted.
fullDescription:
F1-E1 is displayed when the electronic range control (ERC) cannot read its onboard memory. A voltage surge, lightning strike, or age-related flash failure typically cause this.

Attempt a 10-minute power-down reset. If the code persists, the control board must be replaced — there is no field-level recovery.

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 10 minutes and reapply power.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: Install new ERC if fault persists.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for board replacement if you are uncomfortable discharging the HV capacitor.
videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool microwave F1 E1 error fix

faq.a: Not in the field. Boards come pre-programmed from the factory.

title: Latch Switch Fault
shortDescription: The control detected a stuck latch (door monitor) switch.
fullDescription:
F1-E6 is a specific door safety fault where the monitor switch stays closed when the door is open, or stays open when the door is closed. It is a hard safety lockout.

Replace the monitor switch after verifying door alignment. Do not defeat the switch to continue use.
symptoms: Door appears closed but unit will not cook

fixSteps.title: Check door
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect door hinges and hooks for wear.

fixSteps.title: Replace monitor switch
fixSteps.instruction: Discharge capacitor and install new monitor switch.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro — monitor-switch work sits next to the HV capacitor.
videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool microwave F1 E6 latch switch fix

faq.q: Can I bypass the monitor switch?
faq.a: No. It is the last-line safety against magnetron operation with the door open.

title: Humidity Sensor Open Circuit
shortDescription: The humidity sensor circuit is open.
fullDescription:
F3-E1 is a specialization of F3 indicating an open-circuit condition on the humidity sensor input. The sensor or its harness is the usual cause.

Reseat the sensor connector first. If the code persists, replace the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug unit, discharge capacitor, reseat humidity sensor connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new humidity sensor if issue persists.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the control board shows other symptoms after sensor replacement.
videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool microwave F3 E1 sensor fix

faq.q: Do I need both F3 and F3-E1 repairs?
faq.a: No — they share a root cause. Fixing the sensor clears both.
